name: pair_device
description:
Add/pair or remove a physical device -- callable any time.

PROTOCOL (the `protocol` argument -- lowercase: insteon, zwave, zigbee, matter, x10):
- Adding a NEW device: ask the customer which protocol it is if unclear. x10 returns a not-yet-supported message -- walk the customer through manual pairing instead.
- Removing an EXISTING device: never guess its protocol from the device's name or model. Call get_device_family (INSTEON -> insteon, Z-Wave -> zwave, Zigbee -> zigbee, Matter -> matter), or just try node_op(delete): it succeeds for insteon and is rejected for zwave/zigbee/matter/plugin with the real protocol named in the error (see DEVICES, Protocol family).
- A Z-Wave controller still running the Legacy (pre-Z-Matter) generation returns a clear error for any zwave action -- tell the customer to use eisy-ui for that controller.

ACTIONS:
- add_by_address (insteon/x10 only -- the only protocols with a customer-readable address): for a device whose own address the customer already knows or can read off the unit. For insteon specifically, ASK the customer up front whether they know the device's address (use this) or want the hub to go into linking mode (use include instead) -- don't default to one silently. Waits (up to ~80s) for the new device to actually become usable before returning, so it's safe to reference the returned device_address in the very next tool call.
- include: always dismisses any stale discovery dialog first automatically (no argument needed, transparent) before doing anything else. Then: 
  - zigbee: no further question -- call it immediately, in this same turn, with no clarifying question or confirmation first. zwave/matter devices likewise have no customer-readable address, so add_by_address is never valid for them either -- but see below for the QR/code question that DOES apply to them before falling back to this.
  - matter/zwave, and insteon once the customer has said they want linking mode (not add_by_address): ask whether the customer has a QR code to scan (set scan_qr_code: true) or a pairing code/setup code/device address to type in instead (set raw_code to it) -- either opens eisy-ui's QR-scan dialog on the customer's own screen (requires client_id) and waits for a new device to appear, returned in new_devices the same way as below.
  - matter with NEITHER a QR code nor any other code: there is no manual fallback -- returns a message saying a QR/pairing code is required, with no on-hub action taken.
  - zwave/insteon with NEITHER a QR code nor any other code: opens the hub's own manual pairing/linking mode and waits for that protocol's own pairing session to end (however long the customer takes), then returns whatever was newly discovered in new_devices (address + whatever name the hub assigned, usually blank -- no separate lookup needed; rename via node_op using that address). insteon's linking-mode window stays open for a full 5 minutes (not the ~80s every other wait in this tool uses) specifically so the customer can link several devices one after another -- say so to the customer before calling (see the blocking-call note below). device_type is optional -- omit it unless the customer already volunteered it.
- exclude (zwave/zigbee/matter only -- insteon has no distinct hardware remove mode; use node_op(delete) for insteon): also dismisses any stale discovery dialog first automatically. Removes a device. Whether device_address is required depends on the protocol -- this is the one place add/remove aren't symmetric, so don't assume. For zwave, device_address is OPTIONAL and should normally be omitted -- the customer identifies the device physically (pressing its own exclude button once the hub is listening), not by name in chat, so never ask 'which device' first; this opens removal mode, waits (same ~80s budget) for the customer to activate the device, then reports which device the hub excluded in removed_devices. Only pass device_address for zwave if the customer already volunteered a specific address. For zigbee/matter, device_address IS required (from DEVICE DATABASE, never guessed) and there is no physical activation window: the call performs the ENTIRE removal immediately and returns status=exclusion_committed with removed_devices already populated -- do not tell the customer to do anything on-screen, and do not call this twice; one call is the whole operation. Zigbee can fail silently at the network layer (the hub only disables the node locally); this call detects that and returns an error (with device_address) instead of a false success -- if you get it, tell the customer the device could not be removed from the Zigbee network and they need to remove it manually from the eisy-ui interface, linking it as /nodes/{device_address} per UI NAVIGATION.

BEFORE CALLING include or a zwave exclude: these BLOCK waiting for the customer's own physical action (or dialog interaction), which they do on their own screen, not in this chat -- up to ~80s for every path except insteon's no-code linking mode (5 minutes, see above). Say your instructions to the customer as plain text in this same reply, immediately BEFORE the tool call (e.g. 'I've put the hub in pairing mode -- follow the instructions on your screen to add the device.', or for insteon's 5-minute window specifically, 'I've put the hub into linking mode -- you have up to 5 minutes, so press the Set button on each Insteon device you want to add, one after another.') -- never 'let me know when you're done' or any variant expecting a chat reply, because there won't be one; the call already waits for that to finish on its own. Text written after the tool call in your reply is what you say once it's already done.

LINKING: any device this tool adds/pairs/removes, regardless of protocol, is a device node -- when you mention it in your reply, link it as /nodes/{address} per UI NAVIGATION, using the address this tool's own result gave you (e.g. new_devices[].address). Never a /plugins/... link -- that is only ever for the plugin marketplace/dashboard/licenses, never for a device (even one a plugin created). For adding a marketplace plugin (not a physical device), use install_plugin/buy_plugin instead.

protocol.description: The device's protocol family, lowercase. Adding a new device: ask the customer if unclear. Removing an existing device: from get_device_family (INSTEON -> insteon, Z-Wave -> zwave, Zigbee -> zigbee, Matter -> matter) or a rejected node_op(delete) -- never guessed from the device's name.

action.description: add_by_address is insteon/x10 ONLY (needs device_address) -- not valid for zwave/zigbee/matter, which have no customer-readable address before pairing; for insteon, ask the customer whether they know the address (add_by_address) or want linking mode (include) rather than assuming. include (add): always dismisses stale discovery dialogs first automatically. zigbee goes straight to the bare protocol-level include call. matter/zwave, and insteon once linking mode is chosen, ask about a QR code (scan_qr_code) or pairing/setup code/device address (raw_code) first -- either opens eisy-ui's QR-scan dialog (needs client_id) and waits for a new device; with neither, matter errors (no fallback) while zwave/insteon fall back to manual linking mode (insteon's own window is 5 minutes, not ~80s). exclude (remove) works for zwave/zigbee/matter only -- also dismisses stale discovery dialogs first automatically; for zwave, device_address is OPTIONAL (the customer identifies the device physically, not by name -- opens removal mode and blocks the same way as include); for zigbee/matter, device_address IS required and it performs the whole removal in this one call, immediately, no window.

device_address.description: The device's own physical address, exactly as shown in DEVICE DATABASE -- never guessed. Required for action=add_by_address, and for action=exclude when protocol is zigbee/matter (that exact address is removed directly). NOT required for action=exclude when protocol is zwave -- omit it there; the customer identifies the device physically and the hub reports back which one was excluded.

device_type.description: Optional device-type hint (add_by_address/include). Never ask the customer for this before calling -- omit it unless they already mentioned the device type unprompted; it is not worth delaying the call for.

scan_qr_code.description: include only, matter/zwave/insteon (never zigbee): set true when the customer has a QR code to scan visually in eisy-ui's dialog, with nothing to type. Leave raw_code unset in this case. Requires client_id. Defaults to false.

raw_code.description: include only, matter/zwave/insteon (never zigbee): a pairing code, setup code, or device address the customer typed instead of scanning a QR code -- passed through verbatim to eisy-ui's dialog, which validates/interprets it per protocol itself. Setting this also opens the QR-scan dialog, same as scan_qr_code. Requires client_id.

client_id.description: Required whenever scan_qr_code or raw_code is set. Copy it verbatim from the clientId field of the <ui_context> block already present in this conversation -- never ask the customer for it or invent it.
